title: Adversus Omnes Haereses
author: Pseudo-Tertullian
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0276.stoa003.opp-lat2, as held by Open Greek and Latin's CSEL.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

passages.original: hic ex occasione qua dictum sit: omnis arbor bona bonos fructus facit, mala autem malos, haeresim Cerdonis approbare conatus est (et) eadem dicere, quae ille superior haereticus ante dixerat. extitit post hunc Lucanus quidam nomine, Marcionis sectator atque discipulus. et hic per eadem uadens blasphemiae genera eadem docet, quae Marcion et Cerdon docuerant. post hos subsequitur Appelles, discipulus Marcionis, qui posteaquam in carnem suam lapsus est, a Marcione segregatus est. hic introducit unum deum (in) infinitis superioribus partibus.
passages.english: This man, taking occasion from what was said, "Every good tree produces good fruit, but a bad [tree] bad [fruit]," tried to establish the heresy of Cerdo and to say the same things which that earlier heretic had said before. After him there appeared a certain man named Lucanus, a follower and disciple of Marcion. He too, proceeding along the same kinds of blasphemy, teaches the same things which Marcion and Cerdo had taught. After these follows Apelles, a disciple of Marcion, who, after he had fallen into [sin of] his flesh, was separated from Marcion. He introduces one god in the infinite upper regions.
passages.notes: "in carnem suam lapsus est" (literally "fell into his own flesh") is generally taken to mean a lapse into carnal sin. The words in parentheses, (et) and (in), are editorial supplements and have been translated.
